Krusader 2.5.0 answers three points raised in the Unraid support thread: a closed window comes back, there is a diff viewer, and the container needs a third of the memory it used to.

## ✨ Added

- **Kompare is bundled.** *File → Compare by Content…* opens two selected files in a side-by-side diff. Until now that menu entry only replied that Krusader could not find any of the supported diff frontends. Nothing to set up: Krusader finds Kompare on its own and remembers where it is.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The container idles at about 250 MB instead of 780 MB.** The X server reserves its whole framebuffer up front, roughly four bytes per pixel, no matter how large the browser window is. The base image sizes that screen at 15360x8640, which is 530 MB of RAM for a resolution nobody uses. The image now caps it at 5120x2880, enough for any 4K or 5K display and any ultrawide.
- **The cap is yours to move.** The new `MAX_RES` variable sits in the Unraid template with a dropdown from 1920x1080 up to 7680x4320. Raise it only if your browser window is genuinely bigger than the cap. Above it the picture is scaled to the window rather than cut off.
- **The Shift-on-function-keys patch is gone, because the base image now carries the fix.** Version 2.4.0 shipped a small bridge patch so that Shift+F4 kept its Shift. Upstream solved the same thing one layer up and more broadly, so Shift+Home and Shift+Arrow keep their Shift too. The patch was built to stop the build the day the base caught up, and that is what it did.
- **The session script has tests now.** `tests/test-krusader-session.sh` runs the real script against a stub Krusader and pins the behaviour below: restart after a quit, no restart after a container stop, the quit-before-signal order, and both spin guards. It runs in CI on every push.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Quitting Krusader no longer leaves a black screen.** Closing the application in the browser (*File → Quit*, `Ctrl+Q` or the window's X) ended the session and left an empty desktop behind, and only a container restart brought Krusader back. It now starts again on its own, so refreshing the browser tab is enough.
- **Stopping the container still keeps your settings.** The session asks Krusader to quit itself before the container goes down, and that request no longer depends on a process ID a badly timed signal could invalidate. Window geometry and the status-bar state survive a stop exactly as before, since Krusader writes that state as it goes.
- **A Krusader that cannot start stops instead of spinning.** Five failed starts in a row, or twenty instant exits of any kind, and the session gives up and logs why. Before, a program that died immediately on every attempt would have been restarted forever.
